issues: Acceptance tests failed because Jest could not parse the mocked @noble/ciphers module files (__mocks__/noble-ciphers-aes.xxx). The mocks are provided as ES modules (using import/export) but Jest is configured to treat them as CommonJS, causing a SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module. This prevents the entire test suite from running.

The jest.config.js currently maps @noble/ciphers/aes.js and @noble/hashes/scrypt.js to the .mjs mock files, which are ESM and not transformed by Jest, leading to the same import syntax error. The config also ignores those mock files via modulePathIgnorePatterns, so they are never used, causing the real @noble modules to be loaded and fail parsing.

To fix the issue, replace the ESM mock implementations with CommonJS versions (e.g., __mocks__/noble-ciphers-aes.js and __mocks__/noble-hashes-scrypt.js) and update jest.config.js moduleNameMapper to point to those .js files. Remove the entries in modulePathIgnorePatterns that ignore these mocks, and ensure transformIgnorePatterns allows Jest to process any necessary files.
feedback: The introduced OCR, date picker, and category features broke the test environment due to improper mocking of native dependencies. Adjust the Jest config and provide proper CommonJS mocks for @noble libraries so the test suite can run and all acceptance tests can pass.
